field_mappings.note: No Segment equivalent. Documents RudderStack's Wunderkind Lambda-based payload format.
field_mappings.function_name: Derived from WUNDERKIND_LAMBDA environment variable via config.GetString(WunderkindLambda); set on lambda.InvokeInput.FunctionName
field_mappings.invocation_type: Always set to 'RequestResponse' (synchronous invocation); defined as constant InvocationType in wunderkind_utils.go
field_mappings.log_type: Always set to 'Tail' to receive execution logs in the response
field_mappings.payload: The inputData.Payload string field is passed directly as lambda.InvokeInput.Payload bytes; the event JSON is serialized as a string within the inputData wrapper struct
field_mappings.input_data_format: Events are wrapped in an inputData struct with a single 'payload' field (JSON string); the Produce method unmarshals the incoming json.RawMessage into this struct before extracting the payload
field_mappings.destination_config_format: The destinationConfig struct contains a 'lambda' field decoded via mapstructure.Decode from the destConfig map; currently used for metadata but the function name is sourced from environment variables
field_mappings.authentication: AWS IAM role-based authentication configured via WUNDERKIND_REGION, WUNDERKIND_IAM_ROLE_ARN, and WUNDERKIND_EXTERNAL_ID environment variables; uses awsutil.SessionConfig with RoleBasedAuth=true
field_mappings.envelope_fields: RudderStack adds rudderId, originalTimestamp, sentAt, receivedAt to every event payload within the stringified payload

error_handling.invalid_json: Returns HTTP 400 with '[Wunderkind] error while unmarshalling jsonData' message
error_handling.empty_payload: Returns HTTP 400 with '[Wunderkind] error :: Invalid payload' message
error_handling.invalid_dest_config: Returns HTTP 400 with '[Wunderkind] error while unmarshalling destConfig' message
error_handling.aws_invocation_error: Parsed via common.ParseAWSError into HTTP status code, status string, and message; logged with structured fields
error_handling.function_error: When Lambda returns FunctionError (e.g., 'Unhandled'), returns HTTP 400 with the Lambda response payload as the error message

config_fields.lambda: Name of the Lambda function (from destination config map; decoded via mapstructure)

environment_config.WUNDERKIND_REGION: AWS region for Lambda client (e.g., us-east-1)
environment_config.WUNDERKIND_IAM_ROLE_ARN: IAM role ARN for cross-account Lambda invocation via STS AssumeRole
environment_config.WUNDERKIND_EXTERNAL_ID: External ID required for IAM role assumption (prevents confused deputy); must be non-empty when role-based auth is enabled
environment_config.WUNDERKIND_LAMBDA: Name or ARN of the target AWS Lambda function to invoke

aws_session_config.MaxIdleConnsPerHost: Configurable via Router.WUNDERKIND.httpMaxIdleConnsPerHost or Router.WUNDERKIND.noOfWorkers or Router.noOfWorkers (default: 64)

producer_details.close_behavior: No-op (returns nil); Lambda client does not maintain persistent connections requiring explicit cleanup

metrics.note: Uses standard streammanager metrics; no Wunderkind-specific custom metrics defined

notes: Wunderkind is RudderStack-unique. Uses AWS Lambda invocation via the aws-sdk-go-v2 Lambda client with synchronous RequestResponse invocation type. No Segment equivalent for comparison. The producer authenticates via IAM role assumption (STS AssumeRole) with an external ID for cross-account security. Events are wrapped in an inputData struct with a single 'payload' string field containing the serialized event JSON. The Lambda function name is sourced from the WUNDERKIND_LAMBDA environment variable rather than the destination config. When Lambda invocation succeeds but the function encounters an error (FunctionError is non-nil), the producer returns HTTP 400 with the Lambda error payload. The Close method is a no-op since the Lambda client manages its own HTTP connection pooling.
